gaps.wanted: The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state the supply weight only.
What the light bar at the right edge of the port side is. The guide's text and its callouts do not name it.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation; it is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The vertical rating label at the right edge of the rear. It is only partly legible in the photograph and is not drawn.
The colour and blink pattern of the fan slot lamps; the guide gives no table for them.
A supply blank cover panel. The guide says a blank panel is installed over an empty supply slot but draws and names none, and no -S variant is listed.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 7 bays (rear 7); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 9: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 17.36 in (44.09 cm) wide, 20.48 in (52.02 cm) deep excluding the fan and power supply handles, 23.69 lb (10.75 kg) with two supplies and the fans (23.69 lb is 10.746 kg, so the two units of the table agree). The width is the body: the table says the outer edges of the front mounting brackets extend it to 19 in (48.2 cm), so the brackets are not part of the body and are not modelled.

colour.note: The front plate and rear panel of this photograph read the same grey as the QFX5120-48Y's; the chassis colour is carried from that device. The photograph is lit warmly and the value is not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide lists the rack mount kit JNP-4PST-RMK-1U-E (four-post, flush or recessed, racks 600 to 800 mm between the front and rear rails) and a separately orderable two-post kit; the library holds no kit contract for either, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 440.9 mm chassis, without brackets.

environment.note: Table 28: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F) normal operation (the table prints 104 F, which is 40 C, so its two units disagree; the Celsius figure is kept), -40 to 70 C in the shipping container, 5 to 90 percent noncondensing, no performance degradation to 2000 m (6562 ft). The July 2023 datasheet says 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) and up to 1829 m (6000 ft); the guide is the newer source and is used.

front-bar.note: A light bar stands at the right edge of the photograph, between about 12.6 and 33.4 mm down and 1.8 mm wide. The guide's text does not name it; it is drawn as decor and recorded as a gap.

gate-1.note: The front studio photograph is orthographic enough to measure: its body, between the left rim and the right edge, is 1428 px wide and about 141 px high, an aspect of 10.1 against the table's 440.9 / 43.7 = 10.09. Scale 3.24 px/mm. Guide figure 6 is a flat drawing used to count and read the printing. The panel is the same chassis as the QFX5120-48Y: every cage opening, fan face and supply handle measured on this photograph lands within 0.5 mm of the same feature on that device's higher-resolution photograph, so its finer figures are used where this photograph resolves less (its lamps are not resolved at all).

lifecycle.note: No end-of-life notice is held and the guide states none, so the device states none announced.

mgmt-labels.note: The upper management jack is printed C0 above it and the lower C1 below it, read off the photograph. The guide's callouts say C1 for item 3 and C0 for item 9 without saying which is on top; the photograph settles it.

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX5110-FANAFO and -FANAFI, Table 15) and the power supplies (JPSU-650W-AC-AO and -AI, Table 19; JPSU-650W-DC-AFO and -AFI, Table 22) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component and each reused as it is from the library by its part number. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay: the supplies' own fans are inside the supplies. No -S (empty bay) variant is named by the guide, and the supply blank panel is mentioned only in the installation text, so no blank is modelled and a gap says so.

port-lamps.note: DRAWING AND PHOTOGRAPH DISAGREE, and the lamps are carried from the drawing. Figure 6 draws a small ring either side of every SFP28 numeral and four rings along each QSFP28 cage in both rows; the studio photograph shows none (unlit light pipes that do not resolve at its scale). The guide's text gives two lamps for each SFP28 port (Tables 12 and 13: link activity, and a status lamp blinking green at 1 and 10 Gbps and steady at 25 Gbps) and ONE lamp for each QSFP28 port (Table 14, and the sentence before Figure 15: 'one LED that shows both the link activity and status'). The drawing's four rings per QSFP28 port are kept because it is the only source of their place, the first as the port lamp and the other three as channel lamps, and the one-lamp statement is a conflict the owner can resolve. The lamp offsets from the numeral (3.0 mm either side for SFP28, 4.1 mm apart for QSFP28) are estimated from figure 6 against the QFX5120-48Y's identical drawing, whose scale anchor is 6.3 px/mm.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 6: the SFP28 ports run 0 to 47 down each column, even above the cage and odd below it, the numeral printed on a line above the upper row and another below the lower row; the QSFP28 ports are 48 and 49 down the first column, 50 and 51, 52 and 53, 54 and 55. Interface names are not printed and go here only: SFP28 ports are ge-0/0/n, xe-0/0/n or et-0/0/n by speed (Table 5), and the uplink ports et-0/0/48 to et-0/0/55, with xe- or et- channel suffixes :0 to :3 when channelized (Table 6).

ports.note: Front photograph, dark cage openings along the upper row: 24 SFP28 openings in three groups of eight (starting at 8.0, 124.4 and 241.1 mm), then four QSFP28 openings at 358.5, 377.6, 396.4 and 415.6 mm. The cell origins 7.5, 124.05, 240.6 and 358.35 mm and the pitches (the registry's 14.25 SFP28 and 19.0 QSFP28) are carried from the QFX5120-48Y's finer photograph, which this one confirms to 0.4 mm. Counts are 48 and 8, the callouts 1 and 2 of figure 6.

power.note: Table 19 (AC supplies): input 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 7.8 A at 100 to 120 VAC and 3.8 A at 200 to 240 VAC; typical 260 W, maximum 450 W. Table 25 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating range -40.8 to -72 VDC, 20 A maximum, typical 260 W, maximum 450 W. The guide's Table 22 gives a DC supply a 4 A input rating and an operating range of -38 to -60 VDC and says one DC supply ships while Tables 7 and 8 and the surrounding text say two; the chassis-level Table 25 figures are kept and the conflict is recorded here and in the pull request. The July 2023 datasheet adds an idle load of 160 W and gives the same 260 W and 450 W, and states AC input as 110 to 240 V and DC as -44 to -72 V against the guide's 100 to 240 VAC and -40.8 to -72 VDC; the newer guide wins.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 3.24 px/mm, checked against figure 9 and its callouts 1 to 12. At the left a 63 mm panel carries the four chassis lamps, the RJ-45 console jack with the USB port beneath it in one shield, the two stacked RJ-45 management jacks, the ESD point and the reset pinhole; then five fan slots numbered 0 to 4 on a 49.0 mm pitch (orange fan faces start at 71.9, 120.7, 169.8, 219.2 and 268.3 mm), each preceded by a strip with its fan symbol, number and lamp; then the two supply slots 0 and 1, each preceded by a strip with its power symbol and number, and at the right edge a dark strip carrying a vertical rating label. Positions are the QFX5120-48Y's, which these measurements confirm.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The guide's figures 9 and 10 draw the fan slots with AIR IN labels (a back-to-front unit); the studio photograph shows AIR OUT with orange handles. The photograph is the front-to-back build, which is the default configuration. Tables 15, 16, 18 and 24 settle the labels: AIR OUT (AFO) with an orange handle for front-to-back, AIR IN (AFI) with a blue handle for back-to-front. The photographed supplies show a black chassis with an orange handle and the AC inlet; figure 10 draws the DC supply with four terminals (V-, V-, V+, V+).

row-pitch.note: Down the first SFP column the two openings are 11.1 to 18.8 and 25.3 to 33.0 mm; down the QSFP28 columns 11.4 to 19.8 and 24.4 to 32.7 mm, so the row pitch is 14.0 for the SFP28 cages and 13.05 for the QSFP28 ones, as on the QFX5120-48Y. The y origin is the photograph's top edge at row 40.

sources.note: Juniper EX4650 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2025-07-16 (copyright Juniper Networks, Inc.; its end user licence agreement governs the software only): the front and rear figures 5, 6, 9 and 10, Tables 3 to 8 (ports, speeds and models), Table 9 (physical specifications), the LED tables 10 to 14, the fan and airflow tables 15 and 16, the power tables 18 to 25 and the environmental table 28. Juniper's studio photographs of the 48Y, front and rear, 1500 x 230 px (ex4650-48y-front-high and -rear-high). Juniper EX4650 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000640-008-EN, July 2023, 13 pages: the CPU and storage, the idle power and the ordering table. The guide is at juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4650/ex4650.pdf and the datasheet at juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4650-ethernet-switch-datasheet.pdf. Both carry a copyright notice and no licence to reuse their drawings, so facts and measurements are taken and no figure or photograph is copied. No mechanical drawing and no 3D model are held for this family (the held Visio and 3D sets under the Juniper intake are MX only). The guide's figures 9 and 10 are flat drawings of the rear and figure 6 a flat drawing of the front, so no isometric is used.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the light latch tongues at the foot of every upper cage and at the top of every lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-slotting-design.md).

vents.note: The photograph shows two staggered rows of round holes along the top edge and two along the bottom, as on the QFX5120-48Y; drawn as two vent strips on a 3.2 by 1.85 mm pitch.
